title: Rav Acha of Akra deAgma
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Sanhedrin 38b — so it is cited in Otzar Yisrael, under the entry Amoraim. Hyman says, with respect, that it made a great error in the plain sense of the Gemara, which says there: “Rabbi Hoshaya said in Rav’s name: The first Adam — his body was from Babylonia, his head from the Land of Israel, and his limbs from the other lands.” The Gemara asks, “His buttocks (from which place)?” and on this Rav Acha said: “[He was created] from Akra deAgma,” and Rashi explains that it is in Babylonia and is very deep. Hyman quotes Dikdukei Soferim’s shorter reading: “And his buttocks from Akra deAgma.”

notes.text: The supplied עגנותיו is understood as עגבותיו, buttocks, as in Hyman’s quoted shorter reading; מא״ר is read as Land of Israel. The alleged erroneous sage entry and the criticism remain Hyman’s; Akra deAgma is a place in that argument, not a new sage identity.

The consulted Sanhedrin 38b makes Akra deAgma the place from which Adam’s buttocks were formed, with Rav Acha giving that answer. Hyman’s exact Otzar Yisrael and Dikdukei Soferim readings remain attributed; no sage bearing this place-name is newly admitted.
